comment: Tests allowed to build an external app reply inline. "deliberate" needs a reason no real app reply would do; "pending" is a to-do that scripts/check-recorded-replies.mjs makes you delete (#1237). "noBehaviour" lists a recording no test replays because Deluno has no behaviour for the call it shows; scripts/check-recorded-replies.mjs fails for any other recording that no test names.

entries.reason: Deluge replies that no working Deluge sends: a reply with nothing in it, with a field missing or of the wrong kind, or an error with no words. #1268 asks every line and branch of the adapter to be proven, and the branches left are what the adapter does with such a reply, so the test answers every call with one of them (after the sign-in or token page, which are recorded). The replies a working Deluge sends are tested from tests/fixtures/recorded/deluge in the other Deluge test classes.

plex.tv's account answers (the account, friends, shared servers and home users, an owner token, and the ratings, favourites and watchlist read with them) cannot be recorded: plex.tv answers them only to a claimed server and a token that names its owner, and the owner decided on 1 November 2026 not to create outside accounts (docs/testing/account-requests.md, 'Waived until an account exists'; #1343). Only plex.tv's own 401 with no token is recorded (tests/fixtures/recorded/plex plex-tv-no-token, replayed in PlexOnRecordingsTests); every other plex.tv answer in this file is written by the test. Plex, Jellyfin and Emby without the account are tested from their recordings (MediaServerClientTests, PlexOnRecordingsTests, EmbyOnRecordingsTests, RecordedJellyfinTests, JellyfinOperationsOnRecordingsTests).

Property tests (#1271): the feed is written by Deluno's own TorznabFeed.Write from generated releases and read back, to prove the reader never throws on any text and round-trips title, size and date. Generated input is the point; no recorded reply can stand in for arbitrary text. Real Torznab replies are tested from tests/fixtures/recorded/jackett.

noBehaviour.reason: SABnzbd's mode=change_cat on a queued job. Deluno sets a Usenet job's category only when it adds it; it never moves an existing Usenet job to another category (keep-seeding moves are for torrents).
SABnzbd's mode=change_cat to a category it does not have. Deluno never moves an existing Usenet job to another category.
NZBGet's editqueue GroupSetCategory on a queued job. Deluno never moves an existing Usenet job to another category.

SABnzbd's mode=addfile with a file that is not an NZB, an empty file and an XML file that is not an NZB: each answers {"status": false}. Deluno adds a Usenet release by its link (mode=addurl) and never uploads an NZB file, so it has no behaviour for these three calls (Sonarr and Radarr upload the file; the link is what the add-url states show). Kept as the real answer if a file add is ever built.

SABnzbd's mode=addlocalfile for a path it does not hold: {"status": false, "error": "file does not exist"}. Deluno never asks SABnzbd to read a file from its disk, so it has no behaviour for the call.
GitHub's rulesets for this repository, not a reply Deluno acts on. scripts/check-branch-protection.test.mjs replays it to prove the check that main and the release tags stay protected (GAT-10).
